chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said: “The wudu of ʿAlī عليه السلام was only once, once.”
As for the report which al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Yaʿqūb, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said: “Two by two.”
And the other report which Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ṣafwān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said: “Wudu (ablution) is two by two.”

So both are to be understood as referring to the sunnah (prophetic tradition), and what indicates that is what we have previously mentioned of the reports, and that they contain that the obligation is once only. Contradiction in the reports is not permissible, and this indicates that.

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the recommended prophetic practice as distinct from what is obligatory
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports or hadith used as evidence
key_terms.الْفَرْضَ: the obligatory requirement in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before acts of worship
key_terms.مَثْنَى: two by two; indicating a doubled performance understood here as sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.مَرَّةً: once; indicating the single obligatory washing

ai.seo_question: Is wudu (ablution) required to be performed once or twice according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the manner of wudu (ablution), stating that the obligatory washing is once for each part, while reports mentioning 'two by two' are understood as referring to the sunnah (prophetic tradition) and extra merit. It reflects a juristic reconciliation of narrations within Shia hadith literature regarding the obligatory and recommended acts of ritual purification.
